SUMMARY

Johnson & Johnson(JNJ-5.73%)reported third-quarter revenue of $25.4 billion and updated its full-year guidance to reflect increased operational sales growth. Management indicated that the company is on track to exceed $100 billion in annual revenue for the first time in its history while targeting double-digit growth by 2030. The company reported a significant GAAP earnings impact from a $5.5 billion talc litigation resolution and strategic acquisitions in oncology and immunology. The Innovative Medicine segment drove performance with high-growth brands in oncology and neuroscience, offsetting certain operational headwinds in the MedTech division related to international markets.

Operator:Good morning, and welcome to Johnson & Johnson's Third quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in a listen-only mode until the question and answer session of the conference. This call is being recorded. If anyone has any objections, you may disconnect at this time. You experience any technical difficulties during the conference, you may press 0 to reach the operator. We will now turn the conference call over to Johnson & Johnson. You may begin.

Ryan Koors:Hello, everyone. This is Ryan Koors, Vice President of Investor Relations for Johnson & Johnson. Welcome to our company's review of business results for the third quarter of 2026 and our financial outlook for the full year. First, a few logistics. As a reminder, today's presentation and associated schedules are available on the Investor Relations section of the Johnson & Johnson website at investor.jnj.com. Please note that this presentation contains forward looking statements regarding among other things, the company's future operating and financial performance, market position and business strategy.

You are cautioned not to rely on these forward looking statements which are based on the current expectations of future events using the information available as of the date of this recording. They are subject to certain risks and uncertainties, that may cause the company's actual results to differ materially from those projected. The description of these risks, uncertainties, and other can be found in our SEC filings including our 2025 Form 10-K, which is available at investor.jnj.com and on the SEC's website. Additionally, several of the products and compounds discussed today are being developed in collaboration with strategic partners licensed from other companies. This slide acknowledges those relationships.

Moving to today's agenda, Joaquin Duato, our chairman and CEO, will discuss our business performance and growth drivers. I will then review the third quarter sales and P&L results. Joe Wolk, our CFO, will then close by sharing an overview of our capital allocation priorities and updated guidance for 2026. Tom Cavanaugh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine, John Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development and Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech will be joining us for Q&A. To ensure we provide enough time to address your questions, we anticipate the webcast will last approximately 60 minutes. With that, I will now turn the call over to Joaquin.

Joaquin Duato:Thank you, Ryan, and good morning, everyone. Our strong performance in the third quarter reinforces our confidence in 2026 as a year of accelerated growth and impact for Johnson & Johnson. In Q3, we reported operational sales growth of 6%, ahead of analyst consensus. And increased sequential growth compared to the second quarter. With 6 strategic focus areas oncology, immunology, neuroscience, cardiovascular surgery ambition, we are leading in areas of higher medical need where innovation can make the greatest difference for patients. Our powerful combination of innovative medicine and med tech expertise strengthens our competitiveness. 29 of our products and platforms now generate at least $1 billion in annual sales.

Our marketed portfolio continues to perform Our launches are gaining significant traction and we are advancing our new product pipeline that will sustain our growth into the next decade. With sales in the quarter of more than $25 billion we are on track to meet our guidance and exceed $100 billion in annual revenue for the first time in our company's 140 year history. As we advance our differentiated portfolio and pipeline, we have a clear path to double digit growth by the end of the decade. In Innovative Medicine, we delivered operational sales growth of 7.9% with 8 brands growing double digits. Let's start with oncology. We are making progress to redefine care from treatment to cure.

In the third quarter, our oncology business grew by approximately 17%. Our multiple myeloma portfolio and pipeline are unmatched with 80% of patients receiving a Johnson & Johnson therapy as part of their treatment journey. We continue to strengthen the body of evidence supporting our recently launched multiple myeloma therapies and combination regimens. New Phase 3 results announced in July demonstrated that the combination of the Gvali plus Talvay reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 89% as early as the second line of treatment. In solid tumors, sales of RYBREVANT increased by 64%. Reflecting its strength in lung cancer.

And by the end of the year, we expect to receive US FDA approval for RYBREVANT Faspro in advanced head and neck cancer, a disease with significant unmet needs. In bladder cancer, INLEXZO has rapidly emerged as a market leader for new patient share. Just 1 year after its launch. Nearly 1 in 3 eligible patients started on an INLEXZO regimen in the third quarter. Demonstrating its growing role in transforming care in high risk non muscle invasive disease. During the quarter, we also invested to bolster our oncology pipeline. We completed our acquisition of Firefly Bio adding a promising new degrader antibody conjugate platform that targets drivers of difficult to treat cancers, including KRAS.

Our ambition is to become the number 1 oncology company by 2030 with sales projected to exceed $50 billion Turning to immunology, we are building on our 25-year legacy to drive industry leading innovation for patients. Tremfya delivered exceptional sales growth of 68% in the quarter, reflecting strong momentum across its indications. In the U.S., it is now the number 1 IL-23 inhibitor in new to brand share in Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis and psoriatic arthritis. And we continue to generate evidence that reinforces Tremfya's clinical differentiation based on the landmark STARS study, Tremfya is the first and only IL-23 inhibitor to demonstrate positive outcomes in axial disease clinical trials.

Including significant improvement in spinal pain, stiffness and inflammation in patients with psoriatic arthritis. This momentum reinforces our conviction in Tremfya as a foundational medicine in inflammatory bowel and psoriatic diseases and our belief that it can grow into a $10 billion-plus franchise. ICOTYDE, our first in class targeted oral peptide for plaque psoriasis, continues to outpace recent competitor launches. More than 20 thousand patients have initiated therapy through nearly 9 thousand prescribers, since ICOTYDE's launch in the U.S. We continue to make strong progress on commercial access with ICOTYDE now broadly covered across all national plans.

Also this quarter, IMDEE was approved as the first advanced treatment specifically for warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia, a rare life threatening disease that causes severe anemia and fatigue. This new indication builds on IMDEE's momentum in generalized myasthenia gravis. And reflects its broad potential across autoantibody diseases. And we continue to pursue next generation therapies, In July, we announced a collaboration with Cell BioMedicines to advance in vivo CAR T approaches for immune mediated diseases. Next, in neuroscience, we aim to transform the future of brain health by addressing complex nervous system disorders. Today, we are the definitive leader in neuropsychiatry. CAPLYTA reached $1 billion in year to date sales making it our 29th billion-dollar platform.

Driven by strong uptake as an adjunctive treatment for major depressive disorder, CAPLYTA is now the fastest-growing oral branded therapy in this space. And last month, we presented pivotal Phase 3 data that showed CAPLYTA significantly and rapidly improved symptoms of bipolar mania. SPRAVATO also delivered impressive growth of 36% this quarter, reflecting strong demand in treatment resistant depression. Now let's turn to medtech where we deliver Q3 operational sales growth of 2.5%. While we fell short of our expectations for the segment, our conviction in our future direction has not changed. Starting with cardiovascular, we continue to invest in heart recovery, circulatory restoration, heart rhythm disorders to address the leading global cause of death.

This was another strong quarter for Shockwave, Our circulatory restoration business, which grew 17%. The ongoing global launch of Shockwave C2 Aero continues to broaden the reach of our intravascular lithotripsy platforms. VARIPULSE, our pulsed field ablation platform, reached a major milestone this quarter with more than 100 thousand AFib patients treated worldwide. VARIPULSE Pro, which delivers 5x faster ablation speed, has been very well received in Europe where it is driving double digit growth. And just last week, we received approval for VARIPULSE Pro in Japan. With increasing clinical experience, we are seeing differentiated benefits from VARIPULSE In a recent retrospective analysis, VARIPULSE demonstrated a 68% lower risk of adverse cardiac events compared to a competing pulsed-field ablation platform.

And in heart recovery, while physician select continued to affect the Abiomed performance we remain confident in the technology and focus on supporting appropriate patient selection. In surgery, we are poised to shape the next era of care through robotics, digital innovation, and advanced instrumentation. In July, the US FDA granted de novo authorization for OCAVA, the world's first stable and integrated soft-tissue robotic system. This is 1 of the most significant med tech innovations we will bring to market this decade. Ottava's unique architecture, automated features, and next generation robotic instruments to help address surgeon needs for operating room space and better surgical workflows.

Its connection to our open digital ecosystem, Polyphonic, turns procedure data into actionable insights for clinicians. We already signed our first commercial customer for OTTAVA, and we are progressing our development program. Our investigational device exemption trial is already underway in inguinal hernia repair. With future plans for indication expansion into urology and gynecology. Finally, in vision, we are advancing life long eye health to bring better sight to more than 40 million people each year. The recent US launch of TECNIS PureSee further strengthened our portfolio of intraocular lenses. During the quarter, TECNIS PureSee and Technis Odyssey surpassed 1 million implants worldwide. Reflecting continued surgeon adoption and our leadership in personalized vision solutions.

We also received CE marking for ACUVUE OASYS MAX 2-week reusable lenses. Expanding our ACUVUE portfolio in Europe. Overall, this quarter's strong results demonstrate the impact of the choices we have made to build a foundation for durable growth. We have sharpened our portfolio to focus on innovation with the greatest potential to change lives. We have proved our ability to grow through a significant loss of exclusivity. Our strategic investments in high growth areas are delivering results. And our innovation engine continues to drive breakthroughs for patients. That is why we have the confidence to say that we will finish 2026 strong and that 2027 will be an even better year for Johnson & Johnson.

I will now turn the call back over to Ryan.

Ryan Koors:Thank you, Joaquin. Moving to our financial results. Unless otherwise stated, the percentages quoted represent operational results. And therefore exclude the impact of currency translation. Starting with Q3 2026 sales results. Worldwide sales were $25.4 billion for the quarter increasing 6%. Growth in the U.S. was 9.1%, 1.8% outside the U.S. Acquisitions and divestitures had a net negative impact on worldwide growth of 10 basis points. Now turning to earnings. For the quarter, net earnings were $210 million and diluted earnings per share were $0.09 versus $2.12 a year ago.

Results in the quarter were impacted by the proposed talc litigation resolution, as well as expenses associated with the Firefly Bio transaction and Cell BioMedicines collaboration amounting to approximately $7 billion. Adjusted net earnings for the quarter were $6.3 billion and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $2.59 representing a decrease of 6.8%, 7.5% respectively compared to the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted earnings in the quarter were also impacted by expenses associated with the Firefly Bio transaction and Cell BioMedicines collaboration. I will now comment on business sales results in the quarter. Focusing on the 6 key areas where meaningful innovation and strong commercial execution are driving our performance and fueling long term growth.

Beginning with innovative medicine, where our financial results reflect the depth of our expertise and innovation in areas of high unmet need across oncology, immunology and neuroscience. Worldwide sales of $16.8 billion increased 7.9% which underscores the continued strength of our key brands and new launches. Growth in the U.S. was 11.1% and 3% outside the U.S. Divestitures had a negative impact of 10 basis points. on worldwide growth. In oncology, starting with multiple myeloma, DARZALEX growth was 15.6%, primarily driven by strong share gains of 5 points across all lines of therapy, with 10 points in the frontline setting. As well as continued market growth. Partially offset by O-U.S. pricing headwinds.

PRAVYCTI achieved growth of 35.2%, driven by share gains across earlier lines of therapy and continued site expansion. TECVAYLI growth was 77.3%, driven by launch uptake and share gains across earlier lines of therapy following last quarter's approval in the U.S. TALVEY plus DARZALEX FASPRO U.S. growth was over 100%. TALVEY growth was 42.1%, driven by share gains due to increased depth of prescribing in the community setting. In lung cancer, RYBREVANT plus lazertinib delivered growth of 63.5%. With strong share gains in the first and second lines driven by continued launch uptake in all regions, along with rapid uptake in RYBREVANT FASPRO.

In prostate cancer, ERLEADA delivered growth of 9.4%, with continued share gains and market growth, partially offset by unfavorable patient mix. Within immunology, Tremfya delivered impressive growth of 68.2%, driven by continued momentum from the IBD launch with 4 points of share growth in both ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease alongside continued market growth. STELARA declined 5.4%, which reflects continued competitive pressures from biosimilars and the ongoing shift towards novel classes. Growth in other immunology is driven by IMDEE and ICOTYDE launch uptake in the U.S. In neuroscience, SPRAVATO grew 36%, driven by continued share gains reflecting strong physician adoption and increased patient demand.

CAPLYTA showed significant growth of 66.1%,, driven by strong continued launch momentum in adjunctive major depressive disorder and continued demand increases across bipolar disorder and schizophrenia. Now moving to med tech. Worldwide sales of $8.6 billion increased 2.5% with growth of 4.8% in the U.S. and 0.1% outside the U.S. Overall cardiovascular grew 4.1%, including 20 basis points related to acquisitions. Electrophysiology delivered growth of 4.4%,, driven by procedure expansion, commercial execution and new product performance. Partially offset by competitive PFA pressures, which were more pronounced in Asia-Pacific this quarter. As well as the lapping of prior-year O-U.S. inventory dynamics. Abiomed saw a decline of 1.5% due to lower patient volume.

There are encouraging signals in the U.S. performance with improvement in the quarter. Supported by acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, and Impella 5.5 continuing to gain adoption. Shockwave grew double-digits at 17.2%,, driven by continued adoption of coronary and peripheral products as well as new product launches, and the reimbursement in the office-based lab setting within the U.S. Surgery saw a decline of 1% including a negative impact of approximately 30 basis points from divestitures. The decline is more notably driven by ongoing expansion of VBP in China, the surgery transformation program outcomes across the portfolio, and Middle East disruption which impacted tender timing and ordering patterns.

The decline was partially offset by portfolio strength, driven by recent innovations such as Echelon 400 and Duo as well as commercial execution in biosurgery. Vision growth was 5.1%, Driven by premium innovation, strong execution and global reach. Contact lenses and other products grew 4.3%,, driven by strong performance in the ACUVUE OASYS 1-Day family of products, further solidifying our leadership position, partially offset by US inventory dynamics. Surgical vision delivered growth of 7.1%, driven by new product innovations, robust demand for premium IOLs and strong commercial execution. Partially offset by market specific factors such as disruptions in The Middle East.

Orthopedics growth for the quarter was 3.4%,, primarily driven by new product launches such as VOLT in Trauma and EMPHASYS in Hips, including strong commercial execution in Velis pull through and knees. Now turning to our consolidated statement of earnings for the third quarter of 2026. I would like to highlight a few noteworthy items that have changed compared to the same quarter of last year. Cost of goods sold deleveraged by 150 basis points driven by unfavorable product sales mix and increased intangible asset amortization expense in the Innovative Medicine segment for intracellular partially offset by the impact of tariff recoveries in the medtech business.

Selling, marketing and administrative expenses were flat as a percent of sales, reflecting consistent commercial investments in the Innovative Medicine business. We continue to invest strategically in research and development, deploying approximately $4.7 billion or 18.3% of sales which includes $1 billion related to the acquisition of Firefly Bio. In process research and development impairment of $339 million in the quarter is related to the write off of Precardia, a non core asset acquired as part of the broader Abiomed transaction. Other income and expense was a net expense of $5.8 billion compared to $478 million of income in the third quarter of 2025. With the change primarily driven by the proposed talc litigation resolution and orthopedic separation related costs.

The tax rate was a small net benefit in the quarter. Primarily related to the positive tax effect associated with the accrual for the proposed talc litigation resolution. More information can be found in our upcoming 10 Q for changes in taxes. Lastly, I will direct your attention to the box section of the slide where we have also provided our income before tax, net earnings and earnings per share adjusted to exclude the impact of intangible amortization expense, and special items. Now let's look at the adjusted income before tax by segment for the quarter.

Innovative Medicine margin declined from 44.3% to 35.4%,, primarily due to acquired in process research and development expense of approximately $1 billion related to the acquisition of Firefly Bio, transaction cost for Cell BioMedicines, and unfavorable product sales mix and cost of products sold. MedTech margin increased from 21% to 22.9%, driven by the impact of tariff recoveries partially offset by increased strategic investments in commercial capabilities. As a result, adjusted income before tax for the enterprise as a percentage of sales decreased from 35.2% to 30.2%. This concludes the sales and earnings portion of the call. I will now turn the call over to Joe.

Joseph J. Wolk:Thanks, Ryan. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. As you heard from Joaquin and Ryan, our third quarter results were driven by the strength of our Innovative Medicine business. This performance more than offset headwinds in certain areas of MedTech enabling us to exceed expectations on both the top and bottom line, while continuing to invest in our pipeline and future growth. We are clear on where med tech performance needs to improve. Specifically cardiovascular and surgery outside The U.S. and are taking action to strengthen results. While disappointing, the underlying fundamentals of the med tech business remains strong, supporting our confidence in the long term for that business.

Across Johnson & Johnson, the drivers underpinning our outlook remain firmly in place. As a result, we are raising our guidance for 2026 versus our most recent update in July. The depth of our portfolio, momentum from new product launches, and upcoming pipeline catalysts further reinforce our conviction in achieving double digit growth by the end of this decade with sustainable growth beyond. Turning to financial metrics and our cash position. We ended the third quarter with approximately $17 billion of cash and marketable securities approximately $45 billion of debt for a net debt position of approximately $28 billion, generating more than $6 billion in free cash flow in the third quarter.

We remain confident in our full year free cash flow guidance of $21 billion. During the quarter, we completed the $1 billion acquisition of Firefly Bio, deepening capabilities in oncology with next generation antibody engineering to address complex tumor biology. As Joaquin referenced earlier, we also entered into a collaboration with Cell BioMedicine to advance in vivo CAR T therapies for immune mediated diseases. Our disciplined approach to capital allocation is principled on prioritizing investments that support key commercial launches accelerating future innovation, increasing our annual dividend and strengthening our pipeline through strategic value creating inorganic opportunities.

In July, we announced an agreement for a resolution of the ovarian talc litigation for $5.5 billion, which is reflected in our third quarter GAAP results. The agreement is conditioned upon the express participation of at least 95% of claimants, and meeting a 95% threshold. Let me now turn to full-year 2026 guidance. As always, our outlook reflects what we know today regarding foreign exchange rates, the broader macroeconomic environment, and other external factors. Based on our year to date performance and expectations for the fourth quarter, we are raising the midpoint and tightening the range of our operational sales guidance.

We now expect full year operational sales growth in the range of 6.7% to 7.1%, which represents operational sales of $100.7 billion at the midpoint or growth of 6.9%. We do not speculate on future currency movements. As of last week, the euro spot rate to the US dollar was 1.12, However, the average rate for the fiscal year stands at 1.15. Based on that average rate, we estimate reported sales growth of 7.2% to 7.6%, With a midpoint of $101.2 billion or 7.4%. Assuming the current spot rate holds into next year, could expect currency to be a headwind. Turning now to other items of the P&L.

Regarding operating margin, we now expect a decline of approximately 60 basis points This is an improvement from the 75-basis points decline reflected in our updated July guidance that included the impact of the Firefly Bio and Cell BioMedicines transactions, which had a unfavorable impact of 150 basis points. Absent those deals, we continue to deliver base margin improvement. As a reminder, our pretax adjusted operating margin outlook also reflects the cost associated with the 53rd week of operations and our previously announced agreement with the US government to improve access to medicines. For net interest expense, we are lowering our guidance to $150 million to $200 million.

We are also tightening the range of our effective tax rate guidance Based on our year to date results, we now expect a full year effective tax rate of 17.0% to 17.5%. Given those updates, we now expect adjusted operational earnings per share in the range of $10.95 to $11.05, or 2% at the midpoint. We expect reported adjusted earnings per share of $11.05 to $11.15, with a midpoint of $11.10, or growth of 2.9%. Excluding the impact of Firefly Bio and Cell BioMedicines transactions of $0.64, reported EPS growth would approach 9%.

As a reminder for your 2027 modeling, we expect Firefly Bio and Cell BioMedicines to have a combined dilutive impact of $1.36 per share on a full year adjusted earnings per share next year. We will provide more details on our 2027 outlook later this year at our enterprise business review. Let me now highlight several upcoming developments that reinforce our growth outlook and performance for the remainder of the year. In oncology, we expect several important data readouts in the fourth quarter These include data for pasaritomab, a first in class bispecific antibody in patients with advanced prostate cancer who have progressed after multiple lines of therapy.

We also expect data for JNJ-6.11 thousand an investigational first in class once daily oral therapy for metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer. We continue to see strong adoption for INLEXZO with year to date sales of approximately $200 million, and expect to build on that momentum with a data read out in high risk non muscle invasive bladder cancer later this year. We also expect US approval of RYBREVANT FASPRO in advanced head and neck cancer. In immunology, as Joaquin referenced earlier, ICOTYDE is off to a strong start, and we look forward to presenting data in psoriatic arthritis later this year.

In MedTech, we expect US approval of VARIPULSE Pro in the fourth quarter, further complementing last week's approval in Japan. In heart recovery, we are taking corrective action to improve Abiomed's performance. We continue to invest in clinical evidence and expect results from the HR PCI PROTECT IV trial in 2027. The trial will have 1.25 thousand patients, 4x more than the SHOCK-III study. This large scale study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of Abiomed's Impella CP pump during high risk percutaneous coronary intervention. In surgery, we are focused on commercializing OTTAVA following its recent FDA de novo authorization.

We expect adoption and revenue contribution to build over time with the goal of establishing Ottava as a significant pillar of our surgery portfolio by the end of the decade. Regarding orthopedics, we remain on track for the planned separation of the DePuy Synthes by mid-2027. I am really proud of the team working to evaluate all separation vehicles and all options are better positioned today than when we announced our intentions with this business. Given the way DePuy Synthes is performing and the momentum Nimesh Nana and his team are generating, we are leaning towards a spin as being the best option to create long term value for Johnson & Johnson shareholders.

That has always been our base plan, and we are confident that it can be successfully executed. We will provide additional updates as appropriate and when there is more information to share. Finally, I am really looking forward to and hope you join us for the enterprise business review on December 8th. At that event, we will provide additional perspective on our 2027 outlook and the key drivers that reinforce our conviction in achieving double digit growth by the end of the decade. Perhaps more importantly, we will highlight our earlier stage pipeline and how it represents the next wave of growth into the next decade. Attendees will also have the opportunity to experience firsthand some of our latest innovations.

Such as Ottava. 2026 is on track for another successful year. Exceeding expectations set at the beginning of the year. We look forward to closing out 2026 strong and setting up 2027 for continued success. Thank you to our colleagues whose dedication and commitment continue to advance innovation improve patient outcomes, and create long term value for shareholders. With that, we are ready to answer your questions. Kevin, can you please open the call for Q&A?

Operator:Certainly. We will now be conducting a question and answer session. If you would like to withdraw your question, please press *, then 2. We ask you please limit yourselves to 1 question only. First question today is coming from Asad Haider from Goldman Sachs. Your line is now live.

Asad Haider:Great. Thanks for taking the question and congrats on all the progress. I have 1 point of clarification. On the double digit growth by the end of the decade, the vocabulary in the press release references the progress in the underlying business, quote, together with strategic investments I just want to be clear that refers to internal investments and not M&A. that is a question we are getting this morning.

And then, Joe, on your comments that you are not satisfied with the med-- with MedTech performance and are taking action to strengthen that growth, Is the implication there that you are now-- you now feel more urgency to add to high growth areas via M&A and med tech do you think that you have the product portfolio today to drive the improved performance you are looking for? Thank you.

Joseph J. Wolk:Yes, Assad. Thank you for your questions. On the first aspect, that is correct. Your view of that being internal strategic investments is what will propel us to double digit growth by the end of this decade. In the coming years with increasing performance. So that is the correct interpretation. It does not assume any inorganic additions at this moment in time. We always are on the lookout for strategic drivers that could complement our business. That makes sense to be in our hands versus where the asset would currently reside but also creates value for the risk we are bearing on behalf of shareholders With respect to the urgency, it is an urgency to fix what we currently have.

We like the portfolio and the construct. That currently exists with the 3 focus areas of vision care, of surgery, as well as cardiovascular. I think you are very familiar and maybe I will even hand it over to Timothy to talk about some of the things we are doing in heart recovery specifically to address that, what I would say is now a stable business, but we want to catalyze back to double digit growth. We are very excited at what is on the horizon for surgery. With the addition of Ottava over time. That will be a significant contributor to growth by the end of the decade.

And then as I mentioned, earlier, Vision seems to be functioning well both the surgery side as well as the contact lens side where we are the market leader. But Tim, maybe you want to offer a comment or 2 around Abiomed?

Timothy Schmid:Sure, Joe. So Assad, ultimately, Abiomed remains a temporary headwind as you saw in Q3, but our conviction in the long term opportunity has not changed at all. The slowdown we are seeing continues to be the same issue we highlighted in the quarter before, which is the study outside of the U.S. Focused on high risk PCI and importantly, we do not view these challenges as structural in nature and ones that will drive a long term impact on the business. We are not seeing any changes in the patient need nor to reimbursement access or any meaningful competitive pressures.

We also have highlighted some questions we have around the study as to whether best practices were used in the study. And so our focus today is really on education and advancing the clinical evidence based to show the incredible impact that has in both saving and improving lives. And so we believe it is a short term headwind. it is important to recognize that in any emerging area of science, there is always going to be debate and discussion. And our responsibility is to continue to advance the evidence base to support in the best interest of patients. And in the case of Abiomed, we are doing exactly that.

And so the short term headwind but we are very confident this is going to be a strong platform for growth for Johnson & Johnson for the future.

Joseph J. Wolk:Thank you. You.

Operator:Our next question today is coming from Larry Biegelsen from Wells Fargo. Your line is now live.

Larry Biegelsen:Good morning. Thanks for taking the question. Joe, I wanted to ask about the 2027 comments you made at Deutsche Bank. On the top line, you said you expect reported sales growth to be similar to 2026 after adjusting 100 basis points for the extra week in both years, which I think would mean about 5.4% reported growth next year. And on EPS, how should we think about your ability to grow earnings excluding IPR and D? And just remind us of how much the Firefly, Sale dilution is IPR&D this year and next year. Thank you.

Joseph J. Wolk:So for this year, the IPR&D dilution is $0.64. And for next year, the combination of those deals is $1.36. And the way I would think about that, Larry, and you-- you have covered us long enough where you know that typically our income growth or EPS growth will be a little bit better than our sales growth. that is how you can think about that next year after adjusting for the $1.36 adjustment. So we will continue to look at margin improvement as part of the orthopedic separation looking more holistically at our business. Some of the advances we are getting with technology and getting us more efficient across all parts of our business.

But that is probably a good way to kind of frame in your thinking now for 2027, but we will be a little bit more explicit on December 8 at our Investor Day. We will outline specifically kind of the components to that. And then even probably provide a pro forma with respect to the orthopedic separation should that occur at some point next year as well as a longer term outlook.

Operator:Thanks Next question is coming from Christopher Schott from JPMorgan Chase. Your line is now live.

Christopher Schott:Great. Thanks so much. Just wanted to touch base on ICOTYDE. So just a 2-part question here. Can you just give us an update in terms of what you are seeing terms of patient uptake as we think about new to biologic versus oral switches versus injectable switches? And then bigger picture for the drug, are you talking about this as a $10 billion-plus asset? But when you think about this very strong launch we have seen so far in psoriasis, you got a number of additional indications pending. I guess, how do you think about could this be a much larger asset than $10 billion as you think the peak sales opportunity for ICOTYDE? Thanks so much.

Tom Cavanaugh:Great. Christopher, it is Tom. Good to hear from you. First, I do want to start by recognizing Jennifer Taubert and thanking her for her tremendous leadership and partnership. Jennifer leaves Innovative Medicine incredibly well positioned as you see from our quarterly earnings. With strong momentum, outstanding portfolio and pipeline, and most importantly, a great team. We are fortunate to build on that foundation she established and I am excited about what is ahead. And, really, what I am excited about is what you are touching on right now is ICOTYDE. We do foresee ICOTYDE to be 1 of our biggest assets. In innovative medicine, and it is off to an incredibly great start.

As you highlighted, as Joaquin highlighted on the call this morning, I think getting into some of the launch performance, you heard it from Joaquin Already to date, we have seen over 20 thousand patients initiated on therapy. With over 8 thousand prescribers or nearly 9 thousand prescribers,, I would say. So absolutely tracking better than some of-- most all launches in psoriatic diseases. I think early prescribing trends is what you wanted to get at kind of as we think about-- and we are expanding the systemic marketplace. Approximately 60% of the patients are systemic naive. So they have not received any systemic therapy.

And the-- roughly, the remaining 40% remaining 20 percent are sourced from orals and 20 percent are sourced from other treatments, most likely biologics as we dig into the data. So I can say, as you are seeing with regards to the launch performance earlier, a bit expansion of the marketplace.
